content.title: About
content.content: Soup‑tortilla is a ready‑to‑eat kit that includes a flavorful broth and a soft corn or wheat tortilla. The product is designed for quick preparation of a complete lunch or dinner, combining nutritious ingredients with convenience.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortilla originates from Mexican cuisine and has been used for over 3,000 years.
Soup‑tortilla often contains spices such as cumin, paprika, and chili that give it a distinctive aroma.
Corn tortillas are gluten‑free, while wheat tortillas are softer and more pliable.
The ready‑made kit allows you to prepare the dish in 5‑7 minutes while retaining home‑cooked flavor.
Some versions include dried fruit or legumes to boost protein and fiber content.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The soup components (meat, vegetables, spices) are rich in vitamins B1, B2 and B6, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain tortillas supply fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many ready meals, soup‑tortilla typically contains a modest amount of added fats.

items.title: Enriched with minerals
items.content: The kit often contains magnesium and iron, essential for muscle and blood health.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The broth supplies fluids and electrolytes, beneficial for an active lifestyle.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat tortillas contain gluten, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared soups can be high in salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Thermal safety
items.content: Insufficiently heated soup may retain bacteria; bring it to a rolling boil before serving.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some kits may include food preservatives; those with sensitivities should choose preservative‑free options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the broth to a boil, add the tortilla and let it soak for 1‑2 minutes. Optionally garnish with fresh vegetables, herbs, lime, or hot sauce. The tortilla can be torn into pieces and used as a dipper.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 3‑5 days and keep refrigerated.
